$comment: Hash of each frozen version's slice in the dump it was blessed from, excluding doc/description/examples (none of which reach the generated output), taken off the parsed dump before generation runs (see lib/dump-digest.mts). Generation fails if a frozen version's slice moves, because its files are skipped and the rest of the tree would be generated against a model they no longer hold. Run `yarn generate:api` and paste what it prints to seed a version. Record $source when you do.
$source: ghcr.io/truenas/middleware:master, middlewared 20260916121445~truenas+1 (digest sha256:1e16889369d785fa6eb8c85df44617afc5b29b0269a21f231678f736302c3b4a, fetched 2026-09-16). Everything the 2026-09-11 seed recorded still holds and is not repeated here; what follows is what moved. **The frozen files did not move with the hashes this time, and that is the change in practice.** The previous two seeds regenerated v25.10.0-v25.10.5 from the same dump they were seeded from. Here the drift would have imported two fresh instances of the unfiltered-event leak into a released version, so the files are left as the marker in them says — generated once, then hand-maintained — and only the hashes follow the dump. Five things differ in substance from the 2026-09-11 dump, in all six slices. Three are models, all on the event side: SharingS3Entry.audit gains GetObjectAcl, PutObjectAcl, GetBucketAcl, PutBucketAcl, PutBucketVersioning, CreateBucket and DeleteBucket; InterfaceEntry gains stp, xmit_hash_policy and lacpdu_rate and loses its index signature; CoreGetJobsItemExcInfo gains errname. The fourth is an event source's own arguments — FileFollowTailEventSourceArgs.tail_lines gains minimum 1 and maximum 1000. The fifth is a method: system.product_type.removed_in goes from null to v27, the only removed_in that moved between the two dumps. Neither of those last two can reach TypeScript — this generator threads removed_in to MethodModel.removedIn and nothing reads it — but both are inside the digest, and so are part of why the six hashes moved. The unenforced removed_in now has a live case: middleware says system.product_type is gone at v27 and this tree still declares it there. Two of the three models are shapes 25.10 does not send: errname enters Job.__encode__ only at 27.0.0-BETA.1 (22fb62c124), and sharing.s3 does not exist at 25.10. The interface fields are the opposite case and the one that decides this seed. A 25.10 appliance does send stp, xmit_hash_policy and lacpdu_rate — plugins/network.py fills them in on bridges and LAGs — and v25.10's own model carries extra = "allow" precisely to let them through undeclared. Middleware 4303dc820b documented them and dropped that option from v27's model — v25.10's still carries it — so regenerating would have deleted a genuine index signature from a released version's type and closed a shape 25.10 leaves open. That is the argument for leaving these files alone; "no 25.10 appliance sends it" is not, and would license the opposite call the next time a field drifts in that the appliance does send. Regenerating would also have turned CoreGetJobsItemExcInfo's drift into divergent payload types, CoreGetJobs*Event.fields retyped to a new CoreGetJobsItemInput — each needing the hand correction pool.dataset.query already carries, to arrive back at the bytes that are already there. MANIFEST.md records both names regardless, because generation computes the 25.10 delta from the dump whether or not it writes those files, so v25_10_0/api-types.ts declares CoreGetJobsItemInput and CoreGetJobsItemExcInfoInput as aliases of the shapes this version really sends, and each of the five patch indexes re-exports both by name — the whole of the arrangement PoolDatasetEntryInput already has, since a patch directory re-exports from the root rather than from its predecessor and a name added at the root alone reaches none of them. Six frozen files carry hand edits in this seed for that reason. New at v26.0.0 and v27.0.0: sharing.s3.force_disable_versioning (middleware b6d3e9c7b2) and truenas.entitlements.facts with EntitlementFactsEntry (97ed87fa3c, which also marks system.product_type removed_in v27 — main.py's _create_api makes a removed method private, so it is gone rather than merely deprecated at that version). The S3 audit enum gains the same seven members on all six S3 models. Five things break. The certificate models are split by role (5c23288187): ECCCSRExtensions, ECCCSRExtensionsModel, ECCKeyUsageModel, RSACSRExtensions, RSACSRExtensionsModel, RSAKeyUsageModel and ExtendedKeyUsageModelInput are gone and eleven role-named types replace them. CSRProfilesModel keeps its name and changes its keys, HTTPS RSA/ECC Certificate becoming the four TLS Server and TLS Client entries. DiskUpdate loses sed (e0a506435a), which DiskEntry still reports. The index signature closes at different places in different versions: at v26.0.0 on InterfaceEntryInput, which is the interface.query event payload and so the leak rather than a backport, and at v27.0.0 on InterfaceEntry and InterfaceQueryResultItem, with InterfaceCreate and InterfaceUpdate arriving there as their own types. And core.get_jobs and webui.crypto.csr_profiles leave the shared base directories, their shapes no longer being identical across versions, so a client that has not named a version cannot reach either. The virt.* namespace and pool.dataset.encryption_algorithm_choices are hand-restored after generation; no dump reproduces either, in any version.
